transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-11
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Reyes (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (OrchardAI Platform Eng), Carlos Ruiz (OrchardAI NetOps), Sofia Alvarez (OrchardAI Security PM)

Summary: quick network snapshot, confirm cutover readiness for private pilot canary, discuss MTU/BGP/egress shaping, finalize next steps for smoke tests and rollback playbook. A few audio hiccups; some words auto transcription confused K-V cache vs K-V cash etc.

Topics: network health, canary routing, kernel/quantization rollback, observability gaps, security signoff checklist

-- Transcript body --
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining on a Thursday, appreciate you squeezing this in. quick agenda — network snapshot, cutover readiness, and next steps. Samir will run through the tech bits.
[00:18] Samir: yeah hey, hi. so I'll start with the numbers — last 24 hours we saw median p95 latency from your staging to private pilot endpoints at ~82ms for 256 tokens, with about a 7% tail bump during the 03:00 UTC egress surge, that's on the canary route.
[00:38] Maya: when you say 7% tail bump, is that measured after batching? our client side does a 16ms batch window, we want to make sure that's included.
[00:45] Samir: good point, the sampling included continuous batching. oh and small note — our KV cache (auto-transcribed earlier as K-V cash) was warmed for the most common prefixes; TTLs were set to 5 minutes for the experiment.
[01:05] Carlos: hmm, 82ms p95 seems ok, but we saw two BGP flaps yesterday between 02:45 and 03:10 which lines up with the tail. i wanted to flag MTU mismatch on one of the peering links — that caused a small fragmentation and retransmit sequence.
[01:26] Jordan: can you expand on the MTU issue? is that something we need to handle in the cutover window or pre-fix?
[01:33] Carlos: network team can set an MTU of 9000 on both sides, but one fabric still defaulted to 1500 so there was a small window of black-holed traffic for jumbo frames. we'll need to standardize MTU and coordinate the change in a maintenance window.
[01:48] Samir: okay that explains the fragments. for cutover readiness we're recommending a short maintenance window, 30 minutes during low traffic to update MTU + validate route propagation. also run a canary surge to watch egress shaping.
[02:05] Maya: our preference is a weekend window but we can do a mid-week early morning if you need earlier. also we need to align on rollback plan — last thing we want is a stuck canary.
[02:17] Jordan: agreed. Samir, can you summarize rollback options and what metrics would trigger an automatic rollback?
[02:23] Samir: yeah so primary triggers: sustained p95 increase >25% relative to baseline for 5 minutes, token error rate >1% sustained for 3 minutes, or internal queue depth exceeding configured threshold which indicates backpressure. the automatic fallback would shift traffic off the private route to hosted endpoints or a lower-capacity dedicated pool, depending on policy.
[02:48] Sofia: quick security note — for the private pilot we still need the HSM/KMS key rotation document signed off and confirmation that audit logs (3 months) are ingested into your SIEM. did Redwood confirm syslog forwarding?
[03:02] Samir: yes we've got syslog forwarding on the private instance, it's sending to the collector you provided, but we need your SIEM team to confirm schema mapping. key rotation — we can support customer-managed KMS; we'll send the key rotation playbook.
[03:18] Sofia: okay please attach the playbook. also for SOC2 we have one outstanding question around retention of request metadata, can you confirm retention windows?
[03:27] Jordan: retention is configurable per-customer; default is 90 days but we can extend. we'll upload a small doc that shows the options and the policy table.
[03:38] Maya: perfect. back to the network — Carlos, are you comfortable running the end-to-end ingress-egress synthetic test that Samir posted last week?
[03:46] Carlos: yep we'll run that tonight. just to be clear about the test — it opens 100 concurrent connections with 64 token snippets, ramps to 1k queries over 10 minutes, records per-token latency and drops. correct?
[04:00] Samir: that's the one. note, in staging we saw a small serialization in the codec path when sequence length jumped above 512 tokens — the runtime selected a different kernel which increased CPU on the host side. we want to avoid that in the canary.
[04:18] Maya: do you have a quick way to pin the kernel selection for the pilot to avoid the jank?
[04:23] Samir: we can pin model variant and quant profile for the canary; that keeps the same kernel. downside is slightly higher unit cost but it buys stability. alternative is to set strict max-seq length limit on client-side.
[04:36] Jordan: let's list the tradeoffs in the runbook. cost vs jitter.
[04:40] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[04:44] Jordan: sorry who was that — i think Maya speaking?
[04:47] Maya: yeah that was me, just background noise — i'm fine with pinning the kernel for the first two canaries.
[04:53] Carlos: another note about egress shaping — we observed token bursts when our batcher released queued requests at the same time after a blackout. could the Redwood runtime spread release slightly?
[05:05] Samir: yes we have smoothing heuristics and jitter windows we can enable for the canary — random small delays to stagger releases. that's in the optimize tool but we can enable it on the instance.
[05:16] Maya: will that affect throughput? we care about tail latency but not if it halves our throughput.
[05:22] Samir: negligible throughput impact for typical workloads. it's more about microsecond-level smoothing to avoid burst-induced queues.
[05:30] Sofia: regarding compliance, can we have a short checklist mapping: KMS, SSO, audit logs, retention, network egress policies. i want that in writing before cutover.
[05:41] Jordan: yep we'll produce a checklist. we'll put it in the shared drive under /security-checklists/orchardai and link it.
[05:48] Maya: cool. timeline — what are realistic dates for the canary and then broad cutover?
[05:54] Jordan: we propose canary on 2026-03-18 with rollback windows the same day, and if all goes well, broader cutover the following week. but we need to finalize the blackout window and your netops confirmation.
[06:06] Carlos: 2026-03-18 works but prefer the 03:00-04:00 UTC. also we will need NAT translation docs for egress IP preservation.
[06:16] Samir: we'll share NAT/eip mapping doc. also important — please confirm the cert rotation schedule. if certs expire during cutover that's... messy.
[06:27] Maya: certs are valid until 2026-09 and auto-rotate but i'll double check.
[06:31] Jordan: okay let's talk about observability gaps — we noticed a missing trace for one shard yesterday; the trace IDs showed up as null intermittently. probably a small instrumentation bug in the private agent. Samir, status?
[06:43] Samir: we pushed a hotfix last night that addressed a race in trace injector; rollout was fine in staging but we haven't pushed to your private cluster yet. recommend we push to canary before cutover.
[06:54] Carlos: push to canary only. we don't want any global push until we've confirmed MTU and BGP stability.
[07:01] Jordan: agreed. Samir add that to the deployment checklist.
[07:05] Samir: noted. will send the checklist and the small hotfix patch id.
[07:10] Maya: one more operational question — what are we using for circuit-breaker thresholds at the edge? our platform has its own but if both are set you can get double-triggering.
[07:21] Samir: our default is queue-depth at 200 per host and concurrent requests 2k cluster-wide. we can expose these in the config so you can align with your platform.
[07:31] Maya: send the default config please.
[07:34] Jordan: quick call out — conversation drifted a bit but this is exactly what we need to lock down for cutover. to recap, action items and owners are in the notes.
[07:43] Speaker 2: (short silence)
[07:46] Sofia: security question — do Redwood logs include full request bodies by default? we want at most truncated body for PII reasons.
[07:54] Samir: by default we do not store full customer request bodies in plaintext; we can configure token redaction and store only metadata and anonymized snippets. we'll include the config options in the doc.
[08:07] Maya: awesome. about benchmarking — Jordan you mentioned a trimmed CSV and latency heatmap? where will that live?
[08:15] Jordan: i'll upload to the drive after this call and link it in the thread. it's a small CSV with per-run p50/p95/p99 and histograms.
[08:24] Carlos: for the canary we will run the synthetic and also a real traffic mirror at 5% for 15 minutes, if that looks good we'll go to 25% for two hours.
[08:34] Samir: traffic mirror is fine. we prefer terminating mirrors at the Redwood private instance so you don't send a second call to production.
[08:44] Maya: ok noted. i have one more question about quantization — we've seen quality drop with int8 on our finetuned model, is there an easy way to test int8 vs int16 in the canary?
[08:58] Samir: yes we can spin parallel variants: same model with int8 quant profile and a higher fidelity int16 profile. run them in A/B with a small eval set. note that int8 saves ~40% in cost but can change logits subtly.
[09:12] Maya: can we include a short eval suite (50 prompts) that exercises the hallucination cases we've seen?
[09:19] Jordan: yes please attach that suite to the shared drive, Samir will run A/B and return quality deltas.
[09:25] Samir: will do.
[09:27] Jordan: okay final recap — Samir to share rollback checklist and kernel pin steps by 2026-03-13, Jordan to upload benchmark CSV and heatmap by 2026-03-12, OrchardAI (Maya/Carlos) to confirm MTU, BGP and blackout window by 2026-03-14/17. security checklist and KMS playbook will be put in shared drive. canary target 2026-03-18 03:00-03:30 UTC.
[09:48] Maya: thanks everyone, this is good.
[09:50] Carlos: thanks. i'll post the synthetic test results tonight.
[09:53] Sofia: thank you, please cc security on the doc.
[09:55] Jordan: will do.
[10:00] Jordan: okay wrapping — we'll follow up with a consolidated runbook and link. cheers.

References shared: /shared/pilot-runbooks/orchardai/canary-runbook.md, kernel-pin-guide-v2.pdf, network-nat-eip-mapping.xlsx

Transcript notes: occasional mis-attribution and auto-caption errors (KV cache -> K-V cash, quantization -> quantisazion) present in auto transcript. Some crosstalk obscured a few short lines.
